tool_args.rationale: Five same-condition observations at one horizon show saturation-like dependence on u_now, but do not identify the mechanism: Beverton-Holt recruitment and a coupled two-layer bridge can both explain this pattern. The flux-conservation and bridge-epidemic signatures make the open-branch discriminating probe the lowest-cost informative next measurement.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit a simple bilinear mass-action model
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The five observations show saturation-like curvature, which is inconsistent with a linear-in-u bilinear law; the bridge signature also leaves open a coupled mobility mechanism.
Plausible from the curvature, but the current data hold x_now and s_grad fixed and cannot distinguish it from the two-layer bridge mechanism.
More measurements along the same conditions are less discriminating than an open-branch probe for the unresolved bridge mechanism.
It is irrelevant to resolving the target-law ambiguity and has unnecessary cost.
